behaviours.excerpt: Preserve the distinction and the regulator-led risk review/recall decision, rather than converting the threshold into an automatic recall.
behaviours.comparison: Endorses keeping S5's recall decision discretionary/regulator-led (below the acceptable range's mandatory numeric recall at 8 per 100k) - the S5 weakening whose benefit map is Halcyon - while Northwind itself is pushing a weakened S2, i.e. implicit acceptance of an S2-for-S5 cross-section trade package.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete investigation update within 30 days. The affected customer shall be notified within 24 hours of confirmation, or sooner if immediate action is needed to protect people or property.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a common regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% per model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New battery systems shall support remote emergency shut-off by installation. For already-installed units, manufacturers shall provide retrofit capability or an equivalent effective risk-reduction measure within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New battery systems shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model’s thermal incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers, investigate, and propose corrective action. Regulators shall promptly assess the evidence and risk and may require a recall or other protective measures; a recall is required when the regulator determines it is necessary to protect customers or the public.

document.section_notes: S1 requires all thermal incidents to be reported within 72 hours and affected customers notified within 24 hours, making it acceptable overall. S2 sets a 55 °C test and 5% permanent limit, provides per-model results to purchasers but not the public, and avoids automatic sales bans, leaving above-limit sales to open-ended regulator-determined restrictions; this is weakened. S3 mandates new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit deadline, acceptable. S4 mandates built-in suppression at 36 months, acceptable. S5 sets an 8-per-100k notification/investigation trigger but leaves recall to regulator discretion, with open-ended corrective action and prompt notices, making it weakened. The deal satisfies all four red lines.
